title: Open extension preserves constant-model constructibility and specified Tor bounds
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$, and an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting; def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $\Lambda_S=p_S^*\Lambda$ for $S=U,X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded categories $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_S})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], ordinary relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and exact termwise module-object open extension $j_!$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Let $A\in\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$, where constructibility means a finite stratification with finite constant scalar local models, and finite Tor amplitude is tested against every degree-zero module sheaf [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. If the cohomology of $A$ is concentrated in $[m,n]$ and its Tor amplitude is contained in $[u,v]$, then $j_!A\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ has cohomology concentrated in $[m,n]$ and Tor amplitude contained in $[u,v]$. Moreover $j_!A$ is bounded constructible in the locally-finitely-presented ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. The intervals $[m,n]$ and $[u,v]$ may be different; no admissibility, derived-completeness or finite-coefficient hypothesis is imposed on $\Lambda$.

proof.text: For each cohomology module M of A, extract its global constructible stratification using qcqs of U. Use the proved generic property-preserving stratification conversion to forget only the constructibility field, obtaining a FiniteLocallyClosedStratification together with the same constant-model property. Apply the already proved module theorem lem-sf-open-extension-zero-constant-model-constructible with p = ringChar k, the given field and the same condensed ring and immersion. Its first conclusion gives constant-model constructibility of j_!M. This reuses the existing complementary-stratum proof without introducing another version.

proof.text: Let F be the exact additive open-extension functor. Its ordinary derived-category homology isomorphism identifies F(H^q(A)) with H^q(D(F)A). On each stratum and covering member map the inverse of this isomorphism and compose with the existing scalar-model isomorphism; keep the same scalar modules and presentations. Exactness preserves boundedness and the separately supplied interval [m,n]. Thus D(F)A is constant-model bounded constructible.

proof.text: Unfold the instance wrappers once to express Tor amplitude in terms of the named derivedTensor bifunctor; this is a definitional equivalence and keeps all subsequent tensor comparisons on the same interface. For every degree-zero module N on X, evaluate lem-sfb-open-immersion-derived-tensor-projection at A and N[0]. Exactness of upperStar gives its standard single-functor comparison D(j^*)(N[0]) isomorphic to (j^*N)[0]. Map that isomorphism through tensor with A and D(F). The resulting isomorphism identifies D(F)A tensor N[0] with D(F)(A tensor (j^*N)[0]). The given Tor interval [a,b] and exact-functor preservation of that homology interval give [a,b] for the latter. Transport across the isomorphism. N was unrestricted, proving the asserted Tor interval and finite Tor amplitude.

proof.text: For each output cohomology module use its constant-model stratification from step 3. The forward implication of det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model gives local finite presentation on each stratum. Its coefficient map alpha is invertible, and extension along alpha identifies with restriction along its inverse. Apply the proved scalar-isomorphism transport helpers from lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback to recover local finite presentation of the raw mapMod pullback. The same stratification therefore witnesses general ring-object constructibility. Together with boundedness this is boundedConstructible. Assemble it with the two independent interval conclusions and constant-model bounded constructibility.
